title: Bread and wine requested
summary: Jesus commands his disciples to bring bread and wine, then tells the multitude to sit on the earth while the disciples are gone.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus commanded his disciples to bring bread and wine.
While the disciples were gone for bread and wine, Jesus commanded the multitude to sit upon the earth.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The multitude sits on the ground as the disciples go to fetch bread and wine.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the bread and wine before they are brought.
The landscape, clothing, and arrangement of the people.

narration.text: Jesus commanded his disciples that they should bring forth some bread and wine unto him.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Jesus blessing or distributing the bread in this scene; that occurs after the disciples return.

title: Bread blessed and given to the disciples
summary: The disciples come with bread and wine. He takes bread, breaks and blesses it, gives it to the disciples, and commands them to eat. After they have eaten and are filled, he commands them to give to the multitude.

explicit_facts.text: The disciples came with bread and wine.
He took bread, broke and blessed it, gave it to the disciples, and commanded them to eat.
After the disciples had eaten and were filled, he commanded them to give to the multitude.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Bread and wine are present when the disciples come.
The disciples receive and eat the bread before the command to give to the multitude.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, number of disciples, appearance of the people, and arrangement of the bread and wine.

narration.text: he took of the bread and brake and blessed it;
he commanded that they should give unto the multitude.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The supplied verses do not identify the person referred to as “he” or quote the words of either command.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify “he” by name from outside the supplied verses.
Do not invent spoken words for the commands.
Do not show the multitude receiving or eating in these verses.
Do not depict the wine being consumed.

title: The bread ordinance taught
summary: After the multitude has eaten and is filled, Jesus teaches the disciples about an ordained person who will break, bless, and give bread, and about doing this in remembrance of him.

explicit_facts.text: After the multitude had eaten and were filled, Jesus spoke to the disciples about one who would be ordained to break, bless, and give bread to believers baptized in his name.
Jesus said the disciples should always observe the practice as he had done.
Jesus said the bread should be done in remembrance of his body, as a testimony to the Father, and that remembering him brings his Spirit.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus addresses the disciples after the multitude has eaten.

spoken_dialogue.text: And this shall ye do in remembrance of my body, which I have shown unto you.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The teaching about remembrance and the Spirit is spoken instruction, not a visible manifestation.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a supernatural appearance of Jesus's body or Spirit.

title: The wine shared
summary: Jesus commands his disciples to drink wine from the cup and give it to the multitude. The disciples drink and are filled; they give it to the multitude, who also drink and are filled.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus commands his disciples to take wine from the cup, drink it, and give it to the multitude to drink.
The disciples drink and are filled; they give wine to the multitude, who also drink and are filled.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The disciples offer wine to members of the multitude.
unspecified_visual_details: The cup's appearance and the manner of distribution.
The setting and the participants' appearances.

narration.text: he commanded his disciples that they should take of the wine of the cup and drink of it,
and that they should also give unto the multitude that they might drink of it.
and did drink of it and were filled;
and they gave unto the multitude, and they did drink, and they were filled.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The command is reported, not quoted as direct speech.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the words of Jesus's command.
Do not depict the wine as blood.

title: Blessing and commandment
summary: Jesus commends the disciples for keeping his commandments, teaches them to continue the ordinance in remembrance, and warns of the consequences of doing more or less than commanded.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus blessed the disciples for what they had done and said it witnessed their willingness to obey his commandments.
Jesus taught that they should continue the ordinance for those who repent and are baptized, in remembrance of him.
Jesus commanded them to do these things and said the obedient are built upon his rock.
Jesus warned that those doing more or less are built on a sandy foundation that will fall when rain, floods, and winds beat upon it.
Jesus blessed those who keep his commandments.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus speaks to the disciples who have just participated in the ordinance.
unspecified_visual_details: The disciples' expressions and the surrounding setting.

spoken_dialogue.text: And if ye shall always do these things blessed are ye, for ye are built upon my rock.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

narration.text: But whoso among you shall do more or less than these are not built upon my rock,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The rock, sandy foundation, storm, and gates of hell are part of the teaching; do not depict them as a separate literal event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not create a storm, collapsing building, or visible gates of hell.

title: Watch and pray
summary: Jesus teaches the disciples to watch and pray, follow his example of prayer, and recognize him as the light.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus told the disciples to watch and pray always lest they be tempted and led captive by the devil.
Jesus said they should pray in his church as he had prayed among them, and that he is the light and has set an example.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus teaches the disciples; no additional action is specified.
unspecified_visual_details: Whether Jesus or the disciples are physically praying in this moment.

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold I am the light; I have set an example for you.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: “I am the light” is a teaching, not a direction to add a supernatural glow.
prohibited_inventions: Do not portray the devil or temptation as a visible figure or event.

title: Jesus turns to the multitude
summary: After speaking to the disciples, Jesus turns to the multitude and teaches them to watch and pray to the Father in his name.

explicit_facts.text: After speaking to the disciples, Jesus turned to the multitude and began speaking to them.
Jesus told the multitude to watch and pray lest they enter into temptation.
Jesus taught them always to pray to the Father in his name.
Jesus said that what they rightly ask the Father for in his name, believing, would be given to them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus faces and addresses the multitude.

spoken_dialogue.text: Therefore ye must always pray unto the Father in my name;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The reference to Satan sifting people as wheat is a figure of speech in the teaching.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show Satan, wheat-sifting, or a supernatural temptation scene.

title: Prayer in families and gatherings
summary: Jesus teaches the multitude to pray in their families, meet together often, welcome those who come, and pray for them.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus taught the multitude to pray in their families for their wives and children to be blessed.
Jesus said they should meet together often and not forbid anyone from coming to them.
Jesus said they should pray for those who come and not cast them out.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus continues teaching the assembled multitude.
unspecified_visual_details: Specific families, visitors, or a separate meeting place.

spoken_dialogue.text: Pray in your families unto the Father, always in my name,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The teaching about families and future gatherings does not narrate a separate gathering scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not add wives, children, visitors, or a synagogue as visible characters or setting.

title: Hold up the light
summary: Jesus tells the multitude to hold up the light he has exemplified, reminding them that they witnessed him pray and that he invited them to come to him and see and feel.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus told the multitude to hold up their light to the world and said they had seen him pray.
Jesus said he had commanded that none should go away, but that they should come to him to feel and see.
Jesus warned that whoever breaks this commandment allows himself to be led into temptation.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus addresses the multitude, who are present as his audience.
unspecified_visual_details: What the multitude saw or felt, and whether any person is approaching Jesus during this teaching.

spoken_dialogue.text: Therefore, hold up your light that it may shine unto the world.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Light is taught figuratively; do not add a literal glowing object or aura.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a new approach, touch, or healing event in this scene.

title: A further commandment
summary: Jesus turns his eyes to the chosen disciples and tells them he will give a further commandment before going to the Father. He instructs them not to knowingly let anyone partake unworthily and to forbid those known to be unworthy.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus turned his eyes again upon the disciples he had chosen and spoke to them.
Jesus said he would give another commandment and then go to his Father to fulfill other commandments.
Jesus commanded that no one knowingly partake of his flesh and blood unworthily when the disciples minister it.
Jesus said the disciples must forbid a person they know to be unworthy from eating and drinking.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus faces the chosen disciples as he gives them the instruction.
unspecified_visual_details: The disciples' reactions and the presence of any person seeking the ordinance.

spoken_dialogue.text: I give unto you another commandment,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The references to eating and drinking his flesh and blood concern the ordinance; do not depict them literally.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an unworthy person or a refusal; neither event is narrated here.

title: Minister and pray for him
summary: Jesus teaches that an unworthy person must not be cast out, but should be ministered to and prayed for. He describes receiving a person who repents and is baptized, and continuing to minister to those who have not yet repented.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus said not to cast out a person who is unworthy, but to minister and pray for him; if he repents and is baptized, receive and minister the ordinance to him.
Jesus said a person who does not repent will not be numbered among his people.
Jesus said not to cast such a person out of places of worship, but to continue ministering, since they may return and repent.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus continues giving instructions to the disciples.
unspecified_visual_details: Any individual person addressed by these instructions, and the appearance of a place of worship.

spoken_dialogue.text: Nevertheless, ye shall not cast him out from among you,
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The conditional teaching about repentance, being numbered, and healing is not a narrated present-tense event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an individual being cast out, repenting, baptized, healed, or received.

title: Keep the commandments; avoid disputations
summary: Jesus urges the disciples to keep his sayings and says the commandments were given because of disputations among them. He says he is going to the Father for their sakes.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus told the disciples to keep his sayings so they would not come under condemnation.
Jesus said these commandments were given because of disputations among them and blessed them if they had no disputations.
Jesus said he was going to the Father for their sakes.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus is still addressing the disciples.
unspecified_visual_details: Any visible depiction of the Father's presence or of Jesus's departure.

spoken_dialogue.text: And blessed are ye if ye have no disputations among you.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Jesus's stated intention to go to the Father is not yet the narrated ascent.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Father or Jesus ascending in this scene.

title: Jesus touches the disciples
summary: Jesus touches the chosen disciples one by one and speaks to them as he touches them. The multitude does not hear his words; the disciples later bear record that he gave them power to give the Holy Ghost.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus touched the chosen disciples one by one, touching them all, and spoke to them as he touched them.
The multitude did not hear the words and did not bear record; the disciples bore record that Jesus gave them power to give the Holy Ghost.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jesus reaches out to touch each disciple in turn while the multitude is present.
unspecified_visual_details: The words spoken privately to the disciples and any visible sign of the power given.

narration.text: he touched with his hand the disciples whom he had chosen, one by one,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The multitude cannot hear the words; do not supply dialogue for the private speech.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a visible manifestation of the Holy Ghost or invent Jesus's private words.

title: The cloud and ascent
summary: After Jesus has touched them all, a cloud overshadows the multitude so they cannot see Jesus. While they are overshadowed, Jesus departs and ascends into heaven; the disciples see and bear record of his ascent.

explicit_facts.text: After Jesus touched them all, a cloud came and overshadowed the multitude so they could not see Jesus.
While the multitude was overshadowed, Jesus departed and ascended into heaven; the disciples saw and bore record that he ascended.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The cloud obscures Jesus from the multitude while the disciples witness the ascent.
unspecified_visual_details: The cloud's appearance, the precise manner of the ascent, and the appearance of heaven.

narration.text: there came a cloud and overshadowed the multitude

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The ascent is explicitly narrated as a visible event witnessed by the disciples.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show the multitude seeing Jesus through the cloud.
